title: Allow dynamic port allocation for hdfs fixture

timeline.message:
Allow dynamic port allocation for hdfs fixture

Running multiple hdfs fixtures in parallel for running integration tests requires
a dynamic port assignment in order to avoid port clashes. This introduces
the ability to assign port ranges to gradle projects that can be used
to allocate dynamically ports used by these projects.

We apply this dynamic port setup for hdfs fixtures used in
:x-pack:plugin:searchable-snapshots:qa only at the moment as
tests sources (rest tests) in :plugins:repository-hdfs still rely on
hard coded ports
timeline.author: Rene Groeschke

timeline.body:
Running multiple hdfs fixtures in parallel for running integration tests requires
a dynamic port assignment in order to avoid port clashes. This introduces
the ability to assign port ranges to gradle projects that can be used
to allocate dynamically ports used by these projects.

We apply this dynamic port setup for hdfs fixtures used in
`:x-pack:plugin:searchable-snapshots:qa `only at the moment as
tests sources (rest tests) in `:plugins:repository-hdfs` still rely on
hard coded ports.

This is a simplified version of fixtures I created before on the gradle codebase 
to deal with similar issues.

Fixes #66377

timeline.body: Merging to unblock others from CI failures.
What's the motivation for having these port ranges per-project? Why not just allocate a single big block for the entire build?

reply.body: I remember we introduced these ranges in gradle too, to make debugging this a bit easier. I don't have hard feelings or strong opinions here. I like the separation between projects though.

timeline.body: From what I can tell `assignePort` and `releasePort` are never used. Is there something that needs to be still wired up?

reply.body: kind of an oversight. I remove this as it's not used at the moment

timeline.body:
Thanks for the quick fix rene. I actually think this framework you built will be super useful for other stuff. In fact, I'm still quite convinced that our test executor issues are related to integration tests spinning up embedded nodes on conflicting ports with the gradle workers as that logic makes not attempt to check that the port is not actually in use.

We have some similar logic that ESTestCase uses to compute a port based on gradle worker id. We should ensure these two implementations don't conflict and we should also make the ESTestCase one more robust to actually check if the port is available. I still think that's the core issue behind our weird test worker crashes.

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/1a8ce8716d2bbca49c123eceb122898502b8a843/test/framework/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/test/ESTestCase.java#L1479-L1504
